We offer a 8-week in-person and virtual program where youth are able to learn and develop new skills. This program is split into two phases, the first phase (4 weeks) consists of food skills training where youth learn the basics (ex. Knife skills, flavours, baking, etc.,) The second phase (4 weeks) is composed of food production training where you will get real-life experience in a commercial kitchen. Youth receive honorarium payments depending on the type of session attended, with the opportunity to earn up to $400 throughout the program.

properties.key_information: Aberthau Community Permaculture and Eco Art Garden (NW Marine Drive between Discovery and Trimble Street). Located behind the Mansion and hosted by Village Vancouver (VV), the garden includes VV’s recently expanded Collaborative Demonstration Permaculture Garden, the WPG Preschool Garden and art/garden projects by our artist residencies. Emphasizing permaculture design elements, it offers fun, inclusive social, educational, culinary, artistic, and cultural activities for community members. All levels of experience are welcome at our weekly garden work parties, including new gardeners (for more info: ACG@villagevancouver.ca). For more information, visit Village Vancouver at www.villagevancouver.ca or email Ross Moster at ross@villagevancouver.ca. The garden is a member of the Westside Neighbourhood Food Network, and is part of the Westside Permaculture Corridor.

properties.key_information: Riley Park Community Garden (RPCG) has a communal model of community gardening — which means we share the work and share the harvest. Harvests are shared among volunteers throughout the growing season, and excess produce is donated to LMNH Food Hub Program. The garden is also an inclusive gathering place for the larger community, reflecting our core visions to improve food security, ecological sustainability and community development. We host various events during the growing season. There are no waitlists to join this community garden — just a willingness to show up and join in the fun of growing your own food. properties.name: Grandview Woodland Community Seed Library
properties.category: Gardening and Growing Food
properties.definition: Seed Libraries are typically volunteer-run community projects that offer access to free seeds, encourage seed saving, and provides opportunity to learn how to grow food and save seeds.
properties.key_information: The Grandview Woodland Community Seed Library offers community members the opportunity to “check out” seeds to grow at home. Members plant these seeds, care for the plants, and let some go to seed. These seeds can be collected, dried, and returned to the library for use in following years. Seed libraries hold a collection of seeds for its members and offer an easy means for people to access seeds for free or at low cost. They can promote food security by encouraging people to keep and exchange seeds from locally grown, open-pollinated plants, while also increasing community engagement with local food systems and overall level of self-sufficiency.

properties.name: Sole Food Street Farm
properties.category: Gardening and Growing Food
properties.definition: Community-supported/shared agriculture (CSA) is an alternative model of purchasing local farm products. CSA members pay at the beginning of the growing season for a share, and in return, receive a weekly harvest box, typically equalling a set value per week. CSAs support your local urban farmer by providing economic support at the beginning of the season, when there are many expenses and few sources of revenue for a farmer.
properties.cost: Prices averaging around $37.50 – $ 38.75 for 20 weeks with a total value of $750 – $775. See website for details
properties.key_information: Our program will run from May 26th to October 13th, with pick-ups every Wednesday from 12 pm – 6:30 pm at our Olympic Village farm gate. You can arrange an alternative pick-up on Saturdays at the West End Farmers Market. Each share includes a variety of artisanal, seasonal vegetables and fruit grown at our innovative urban farm social enterprise. Every week, our farmers harvest ecologically grown produce and assemble a $36-value share for you. While weekly amounts may vary, over the season, you’ll receive produce equal to—or greater than—your total share investment. Here is a sample of what to expect in your share throughout the season: Spring: chard, cabbage, fennel, turnips, lettuce, radish, cardoon, purplette onions Summer: cherry tomatoes, zucchini, beets, beans, cucumbers, chard, dill, garlic Fall: cabbage, potatoes, carrots, leeks, winter squash, daikon, hot peppers

properties.name: Cottonwood Community Garden
properties.category: Gardening and Growing Food
properties.definition: A food system modelled on woodland forest ecosystems and companion planting. It involves growing a succession of layers that are found naturally in forests. It creates a regenerative and permanent ecosystem resulting in carbon sequestration. The food forests are integrated into social spaces where people from diverse backgrounds can co-learn together while honouring Indigenous and first-generation migrant plant knowledge.
properties.target: Community members - individual plots and common area food forest growing
properties.key_information: Cottonwood Community Garden is a volunteer-managed community garden in East Vancouver. The Garden includes 120 garden plots and 2 acres of communal spaces, including a Native Plant Garden and an Asian Plant Garden. Cottonwood was started in 1991 when community activists reclaimed an industrial waste site. We continue to advocate for health and wellbeing through gardening and stewarding the land on Vancouver's Eastside.

properties.category: Gardening and Growing Food
properties.definition: Various types of gardening programs
properties.target: This program is open to registered DIGA members only. Online member registration is free and available on this website.
properties.key_information: Operating in Metro Vancouver BC, we offer workshops, garden tours, customized adaptive tools, and our volunteers work one-on-one with DIGA members tending to fully accessible plots in community gardens. Our community gardens have wheelchair-accessible pathways and raised beds. Many also offer roll-under table-top gardens. DIGA is currently a part of 7 community gardens around Metro Vancouver. We proudly support these gardens as we work to together to make gardening more accessible for all. Each garden is conveniently located near accessible facilities and public transit.

properties.name: Sky Harvest
properties.category: Gardening and Growing Food
properties.definition: Are distinguished from other food growing and urban agriculture initiatives in that the food is grown for sale and/or profit.
properties.key_information: Sky Harvest grows high-quality organic microgreens and specialty greens for restaurants and retail in Vancouver. Our Richmond based farm is Canada’s first Certified Organic urban farm, and our greens are delivered by bike to local customers. We grow approximately fifteen varieties of fresh microgreens with a wide range of flavours, colours, textures and a high nutritional value. Please note, curbside pick-up through the farm is available for confirmed orders from an online purchase only. We do not have a retail storefront on-site so please order in advance In-store pickup or delivery across Metro Vancouver. Also curbside pick-up from the farm or delivery in our bike zone. Check website for locations

properties.name: UBC Botanical Garden
properties.address: 6804 SW Marine Drive Vancouver, BC V6T 1Z4
properties.category: Gardening and Growing Food
properties.definition: Are distinguished from other food growing and urban agriculture initiatives in that the food is grown for sale and/or profit.
properties.key_information: The Food Garden is a formal space where visitors are encouraged to explore our connection to food through display and demonstration. Partially enclosing the garden are espalier trained apple and pear trees. Within the espalier screen, soft fruits are grown in ground-level beds surrounding a series of raised beds where vegetables and culinary herbs are cultivated. The raised beds allow the soil to heat up earlier in the spring, provide needed drainage and are easier to work than ground-level beds. The Food Garden is managed by the Garden’s professional gardening staff, and the produce is picked by volunteer Friends of the Garden (FOGs), packed in the garden and shipped to an organization on Vancouver’s Downtown Eastside where it benefits the hungry and homeless.

properties.name: Renfrew Collingwood Food Justice / Neighbourhood House - Community Care CSA
properties.category: Gardening and Growing Food
properties.definition: Community-supported/shared agriculture (CSA) is an alternative model of purchasing local farm products. CSA members pay at the beginning of the growing season for a share, and in return, receive a weekly harvest box, typically equalling a set value per week. CSAs support your local urban farmer by providing economic support at the beginning of the season, when there are many expenses and few sources of revenue for a farmer.
properties.cost: For $40 a week over 10 weeks (for a total of $400), you receive a full CCHB share each week. (This will be $25.00 worth of vegetables weekly, with the remaining cost going to subsidize the box of a low-income neighbour.)
properties.key_information: Sign up to receive a Community Care Harvest Box share of fresh, locally grown veggies from our Fresh Roots schoolyard farms while also helping a low-income neighbour access a share at a subsidized rate. Commit for one or both 10-week sessions - May 31st to August 2nd (Session 1) or August 9th to October 11th (Session 2). Pick-up will be from 4 to 6pm on Fridays at 5288 Joyce St.

properties.name: Gordon Neighbourhood House - Urban Gardening
properties.category: Gardening and Growing Food
properties.definition: Provide demonstration gardening, workshops and other environmental education programs to encourage the involvement of community members in gardening activities, including schools and youth groups.
properties.key_information: Come get your hands dirty with us. Gordon House operates multiple volunteer-led urban garden plots across the West End. properties.name: Renfrew Collingwood Food Justice - Norquay Community Food Forest
properties.category: Gardening and Growing Food
properties.definition: A food system modelled on woodland forest ecosystems and companion planting. It involves growing a succession of layers that are found naturally in forests. It creates a regenerative and permanent ecosystem resulting in carbon sequestration. The food forests are integrated into social spaces where people from diverse backgrounds can co-learn together while honouring Indigenous and first-generation migrant plant knowledge.
properties.key_information: RCFJ supports and stewards the Norquay Community Food Forest. The Food Forest is a hidden gem nestled between houses at 2732 Horley St. It is home to a variety of fruit-bearing, edible, and medicinal native plants as well as a composter, a swing, and a seating area for events and workshops.

properties.name: Trout Lake Medicine Wheel Garden
properties.category: Gardening and Growing Food
properties.definition: A place open to the public, operated or overseen by non-profit societies, where members grow and maintain edible and ornamental plants. In most cases the food is for the members who grow the food.
properties.key_information: This medicine wheel garden was created in 2017. It was built by the Cedar Cottage Food Network in partnership with Vancouver Park Board and Trout Lake Community Centre. A medicine wheel is an indigenous teaching that shows the inter-connectivity of different parts of life in relation with the nature and the spiritual world. The design consists of four different parts that represent directions, elements, seasons, or nations among many others. Traditionally, the medicine wheel is used for ceremonious, religious, and healing purposes, or to illustrate cultural concepts. The garden is now a learning garden where we grow native and medicinal plants for the community and held workshops.

Owned and operated by local chefs Andrea Carlson and Gabriella Meyer, the shop also provides a pick up location for Community Supported Agriculture (CSA) bags. properties.name: City Beet Farm
properties.category: Gardening and Growing Food
properties.definition: Community-supported/shared agriculture (CSA) is an alternative model of purchasing local farm products. CSA members pay at the beginning of the growing season for a share, and in return, receive a weekly harvest box, typically equalling a set value per week. CSAs support your local urban farmer by providing economic support at the beginning of the season, when there are many expenses and few sources of revenue for a farmer.
properties.target: Homeowners receive a weekly box of vegetables in exchange for the use of their land and we sell the rest through a Community Supported Agriculture model.
properties.key_information: Participation in Community Supported Agriculture (CSA); grow organic vegetables on front and back yards. Our aim is to have 7-10 items in the share per week, and for the average weekly value to be $35. Most of our share members tend to be from households of two to four people and report that they're satisfied with the volume of veggies they're getting! We plan for the share to last 20 weeks, but if we end up with a few higher value pickups it might go to 18 or 19 weeks instead-- we'll let you know once the final weeks are in sight. From June through October, every Wednesday evening from 4:00-6:30 pm, we are set up outside of the lovely Federal Store Luncheonette and Grocer at the corner of 10th Ave and Quebec St for veggie and flower CSA pick-ups. We also set up a market table right next to CSA pickup, so we welcome non-members to stop by and check out what is seasonally available.

properties.name: Cedar Cottage Medicine Wheel Garden
properties.category: Indigenous Food Programs
properties.definition: Indigenous gardens aim to serve educational and research needs related to Indigenous knowledge and its intersections with other ways of knowing. Typically focused on Indigenous food sovereignty, food security, and traditional plant knowledge.
properties.key_information: Located in Trout Lake Park, it was built by the Cedar Cottage Food Network in partnership with Vancouver Park Board and Trout Lake Community Centre. A medicine wheel is an indigenous teaching that shows the inter-connectivity of different parts of life in relation with the nature and the spiritual world. The design consists of four different parts that represent directions, elements, seasons, or nations among many others. Traditionally, the medicine wheel is used for ceremonious, religious, and healing purposes, or to illustrate cultural concepts.

properties.name: Ancestral FoodWays
properties.category: Indigenous Food Programs
properties.definition: Indigenous gardens aim to serve educational and research needs related to Indigenous knowledge and its intersections with other ways of knowing. Typically focused on Indigenous food sovereignty, food security, and traditional plant knowledge.
properties.key_information: Ancestral FoodWays Collective Society envisions an intercultural future of Indigenous Food Sovereignty, where the Biocultural Heritage of this land is protected, held in sovereignty by Indigenous communities, with thriving ancestral food systems in place to sustain and hold up Indigenous knowledge and lived experiences. We are working towards a world where Indigenous solidarity economies flourish within corridors of biocultural interconnection: where humans and the more-than-human find nourishment, shelter, and healing within abundant and diverse ecosystems of land, water, and food. Central to this vision is the empowerment of the next generation, ensuring they are equipped with the critical knowledge, practices, skills and resources to navigate and address the challenges of the modern world while honoring and perpetuating their cultural heritage.

properties.key_information: The Farmers’ Market Nutrition Coupon Program is a healthy eating initiative that supports farmers’ markets and strengthens food security across British Columbia. Coupons can be spent at BC Farmers’ Markets that participate in the coupon program, and can be used to purchase vegetables, fruits, nuts, eggs, dairy, herbs, vegetable and fruit plants, honey, meat and fish. Households enrolled in the program may receive up to $27 per week in coupons for up to 16 weeks. The amount, frequency and duration can vary according to each partner’s program guidelines and the length of the Farmer’s Market season in the community. You must get in touch with your local community partner directly. Please note that there is high demand and limited funding for this program across BC, and capacity will vary from partner to partner.

properties.key_information: The Cedar Cottage Food Network is an independent, non-profit organization working toward more sustainable and just food systems at the neighbourhood level. Our programs happen in the Kensington-Cedar Cottage (KCC) neighbourhood in Vancouver. Mission Cedar Cottage Food Network creates space for KCC residents to take part in different levels of food systems by providing programming, tools, and opportunities for community connections. Current Program: This medicine wheel garden was created on September 24, 2017. It was built by the Cedar Cottage Food Network in partnership with Vancouver Park Board and Trout Lake Community Centre. A medicine wheel is an indigenous teaching that shows the inter-connectivity of different parts of life in relation with the nature and the spiritual world. The design consists of four different parts that represent directions, elements, seasons, or nations among many others. Traditionally, the medicine wheel is used for ceremonious, religious, and healing purposes, or to illustrate cultural concepts.

properties.key_information: Catering and product....At Ayapacha, we are driven by the profound significance of connection – to our roots, our community, ourselves, and our Pachamama (Mother Earth). The word ‘Aya’ embodies spirit or energy, resonating deeply with our team as we recognize and value every vibration and frequency present in all living things. Similarly, ‘Pacha’ represents all that surrounds us, emphasizing the interconnectedness shared among us through the energies that encompass our environment. In Andean culture, mountains are revered as gods, known as ‘Apu,’ while the sun, ‘Inti,’ symbolizes life. We draw parallels between the dedication required to scale a mountain and the craftsmanship behind each dish. Ayapacha extends beyond food; we aim to cultivate a community centered around health, sustainability, and a deep connection to nature. Our ‘Seed to Soul Journey’ narrates the transformation of food from seed to nourishment, highlighting the interconnectedness between humans, nature, and the food we consume.

properties.key_information: les amis du FROMAGE is a family owned and operated specialty cheese store with two locations in Vancouver. With a carefully curated selection of local and imported cheeses, charcuterie and accompaniments, we also specialize in frozen soups and meals, all made in house using top quality ingredients. Founded in 1985, les amis du FROMAGE is proud to still remain a family owned and operated Vancouver company after over 30 years in business. Current owners Allison Spurrell and Joe Chaput have come a long way since the original shoe-box sized store opened in Vancouver’s Point Grey neighbourhood. You can rest assured that their mission is to continue the company’s reputation of offering the highest quality cheeses, cut to order, along with one-to-one customer service. les amis du FROMAGE is honoured to have been voted “Best Cheese Shop” by readers of The Georgia Straight, The Westender and The Courier, and has been awarded Vancouver Magazine’s Restaurant Award for Top Food Supplier to Vancouver’s best restaurants and hotels.

Taken over by Rick Freeman in 1985, the butcher shop has mostly recently been passed to his son Connor in 2009. Since 1946, Windsor Quality Meats have been proud to be The Meat Men on Main. Friendly, helpful men with cleavers who wrap up your order in (recyclable) paper and send you off with a smile, knowing you’re getting the top-notch, award-winning product that the finest chefs in town insist on. That’s why we’ve won many Best Vancouver Butcher awards over the years.

properties.key_information: Egyptian Bites was born out of Rehab Elsayed's heartfelt longing for the authentic flavours of Egypt. Inspired by the traditional foods of her homeland, Rehab has become a master in the craft of making feteer, a flaky pastry delicacy deeply woven into Egyptian culinary history. Her delectable feteers, whether generously filled with savoury vegetables and meat or adorned with honey, molasses, or cheese, have left a lasting impression on many.

Proud member of the Dream Cuisines alumni, Vijaya celebrates strong women in the culinary world.

properties.key_information: Hello! My name is Huda. I came to Canada six years ago, and I find it a very beautiful country. Egyptian food is not popular or well-known in Vancouver, so I decided to present my culture through cuisine. It was not until I came here that I became very proud of my Egyptian culture, which is vibrant, historic, and one of the most ancient in the world. I’m excited to introduce my culture with pride, by sharing my food with my new welcoming and diverse community. The smell of food in the oven reminds me of my childhood, and makes me happy—it’s a way to bring back lost days, and create a new sense of home. I cook Egyptian dishes like my mom did, filled with love and bursting with flavours. I’m looking forward to having you try my dishes: all high quality, and made fresh and by hand.

properties.key_information: La Win Supermarket stands out as a vibrant addition to the Vancouver community, providing an exceptional selection of Asian grocery items that cater to diverse culinary needs. Customers have expressed their delight in discovering a variety of vegetarian options, seasonal produce, and fresh meats, alongside an impressive bakery section renowned for its Japanese-style fluffy bread and matcha products. The store's unique offerings include specialty drinks, like Craft Boss Matcha Latte and Kirin Salty Lychee Drink, reminiscent of those found in Japanese convenience stores. La Win Supermarket is not just a grocery store; it is a culinary destination that enriches the local community with its diverse range of products and a welcoming environment, making it a must-visit for anyone in search of authentic Asian ingredients.

properties.key_information: Catering and product....At Ayapacha, we are driven by the profound significance of connection – to our roots, our community, ourselves, and our Pachamama (Mother Earth). The word ‘Aya’ embodies spirit or energy, resonating deeply with our team as we recognize and value every vibration and frequency present in all living things. Similarly, ‘Pacha’ represents all that surrounds us, emphasizing the interconnectedness shared among us through the energies that encompass our environment. In Andean culture, mountains are revered as gods, known as ‘Apu,’ while the sun, ‘Inti,’ symbolizes life. We draw parallels between the dedication required to scale a mountain and the craftsmanship behind each dish. Ayapacha extends beyond food; we aim to cultivate a community centered around health, sustainability, and a deep connection to nature. Our ‘Seed to Soul Journey’ narrates the transformation of food from seed to nourishment, highlighting the interconnectedness between humans, nature, and the food we consume.

Now in Canada, her culinary journey continues to bring people together, putting smiles on everyone’s faces.

Empanada Gal has evolved over the years and Carmen has been creating new recipes while incorporating classic ones. Carmen had a vision and over time, that vision became reality and now she produces amazing food with passion that connects with the community! Empanada Gal goes above and beyond! From Guatemalan Tamales, to our hand-crafted dipping sauces, we evolve and customize our selection to celebrate special occasions and holidays!
